## Results & robustness
All methods are tested on the same 9 stress scenarios x 3 forecast-noise seeds (27 cases), through the same safety layer. The **hybrid LP-DQN** keeps the pond healthier and handles the drought best; raw energy differs by under 1% between the good methods (the pond holds only about 0.4 day of flow), so the story is *storage, drought handling and robustness*.  
_Modelled study dataset (not observed CEB telemetry) - decision support only._

panels.title: Hybrid score
panels.description: Higher is better (energy minus penalties for spill, reserve, river shortfall, year-end shortfall).

panels.title: Upper-bound score
panels.description: Knows the future inflow: not deployable, shows the ceiling.

panels.title: Safety violations
panels.description: Across all evaluation runs of every method: 0 floor breaches and 0 mass-balance violations.

panels.title: Composite score (higher is better)
panels.description: Demand-weighted energy minus penalties for spill, reserve breaches, river-release shortfall and year-end shortfall.

panels.title: Storage left at year end (MCM, target 0.835)
panels.description: The old DQN ended the year empty; every v2 method keeps the reserve, the rolling LP and hybrid also approach the 50% target.

panels.title: Avoidable spill (MCM)
panels.description: Water spilled while the turbines could have taken it (lower is better).

panels.title: Days with river-release shortfall (mean per case)
panels.description: Environmental / irrigation release that could not be met (mostly in the drought scenario).

panels.title: Days below the 20% reserve (% of days)
Decision time (ms per decision)
panels.description: All methods decide in a few milliseconds - fast enough for real-time use.

panels.title: Full scoreboard
panels.description: Mean over 9 scenarios x 3 forecast-noise seeds, initial storage 50%.

panels.title: Where each method wins or loses (composite score by scenario)
Scenario x method heat-map (composite score)
panels.description: Green = better. The El Nino drought separates the methods most; in normal scenarios they are close.

panels.title: Robustness across training seeds (5 hybrid seeds, 4 DQN seeds)
Mean and spread across training seeds
panels.description: Standard deviation across independently trained models: the hybrid is steady, the plain DQN varies more.

panels.title: Paired test against the rolling LP (positive = better)
panels.description: Hybrid beats the rolling LP in all 5 seeds on energy and river shortfall; plain DQN does not.

panels.title: Composite score of every trained model (one bar per training seed)
panels.description: Each bar is one independently trained model on the same 27 test cases.

panels.title: Policy adaptation (regime shift: drought + biased forecasts from day 150)
Composite score after the regime shift (higher is better)
panels.description: Hybrid with online fine-tuning vs frozen hybrid vs the rolling LP.

panels.title: Fine-tuning rounds (accepted only if safe)
panels.description: A fine-tuned model is deployed only if it helps on the last 60 days and does not lose more than 6 points on the guard scenarios.

panels.title: Validation score during training (mean of seeds, with lowest/highest seed)
panels.description: Validation score during training; hybrid (green) versus plain DQN (red), solid = mean over training seeds, dashed = lowest and highest seed.

panels.title: Hard-constraint audit over all evaluation runs
panels.description: Every method, every scenario: the 204.00 masl floor was never breached and water balance always closed.
